verdict.what: a brick tavern or frontier saloon with a stone plinth
verdict.style: rustic frontier brick with stone base and green copper-style trim
verdict.looks: A boxy, slightly tapered two-storey shell on a grey stone-brick plinth. Red brick walls with dark stone-brick pillars at the corners and along the sides. The front has a wide open doorway framed by grey stone, with a lit interior of wooden planks, barrels, and lanterns on either side. Green (oxidised-copper) blocks form a flat band along the roof edge, with dark stone crenellation-like merlons and small orange-red blocks sticking out at the corners. The side wall has large gaps, including a missing window section and open patches where bricks are absent, plus a few orange blocks floating at odd angles. The back is a plain, mostly unbroken brick wall under a green roof band, with orange stray blocks on the edges. Rod-like lightning rods top the corners.
verdict.summary: A good brick-and-stone tavern base with a nice lit interior, but the side wall has real holes, the orange trim blocks float off the facade, and the green roof reads as a flat lid, so it needs repair before anyone places it.
